about: Chat and completion list prices for runner/pricing/model-pricing.ts, which reads this file. Embedding prices stay in runner/pricing/embedding-pricing.ts.

One row per provider:model id. cache_write is the 5-minute prompt-cache write rate; Anthropic 1-hour writes bill 2x input (ANTHROPIC_CACHE_WRITE_1H_MULT). cache_read is the prompt-cache hit rate. null means no rate is modelled, and consumers fall back to input.
long_prompt, where present, applies to the whole request once its prompt (input plus cache reads and writes) is more than threshold_tokens; exactly threshold_tokens pays the base row.

source_basis says where source_url and source_date came from: row (the comment on this row in model-pricing.ts before 2026-11-04), ledger (the same price and its check date in runner/ledger/budget-ledger.ts), file-header (model-pricing.ts header: verified 2026-07-26), supplied (the code named no source; provider pricing page and the table date).
A price change is a new dated file, never an edit to this one.
fetched (from 2026-11-08) means the change that added the row read the rate from source_url on source_date.

tool_fees (from 2026-11-15) are the per-call fees a provider bills for a server-side web tool on top of tokens, in USD per 1,000 calls, keyed provider:tool. The metering proxy charges them on install slots only (runner/proxy/hosted-tools.ts). A hosted web tool with no row here is refused on an install slot (HE-PROXY-011), never metered at $0.

rate_change, where present, holds the rates a row bills from its date (from, YYYY-MM-DD) on: the metering proxy prices each request at the rates of the UTC day it reaches the proxy (model-pricing.ts priceOnDate). The row's own rates hold before that day.

tool_fees.note: Web search tool: $10 per 1,000 searches plus token costs for the results; each search counts once whatever it returns, and a search that fails with an error is not billed. Reported as usage.server_tool_use.web_search_requests. Every web_search_ tool version bills the same.
Web fetch tool: no additional charges beyond standard token costs for the fetched content. Reported as usage.server_tool_use.web_fetch_requests, counted at $0.

Responses tool type web_search (incl. images): $10.00 per 1,000 calls plus search content tokens at model rates, which the response usage already counts. Each web_search_call output item is one call. web_search_preview has no row: it bills $10 per 1,000 calls on reasoning models and $25 on other models, and the proxy cannot tell which applies, so an install slot refuses it.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (OpenRouter canonical slug deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-20261017) on OpenRouter's DeepSeek endpoint only (tag deepseek), the one endpoint the metering proxy lets a request reach: provider.only ["deepseek"], allow_fallbacks false and max_price at this row's input and output rates. These are that endpoint's peak list rates, input $0.30, output $1.20 (reasoning tokens bill as output) and cache hits $0.006 per million tokens. DeepSeek bills half on weekends and in off-peak UTC hours, and the proxy cannot see which period a request got, so metered spend is an upper bound; OpenRouter's own usage.cost is recorded beside each request for reconciliation. Other providers OpenRouter lists for this model are cheaper or dearer, and none of them is priced here.

Paid tier, standard. Google lists $2, $10 and $0.10 context caching through 2026-11-30 and $4, $20 and $0.20 from 2026-12-01. Implicit caching only, so no cache write is billed. Thinking tokens bill as output.

Google AI Studio's standard endpoint (tag google-ai-studio, provider Google AI Studio, standard tier), the one the metering proxy pins since 2026-11-16, at the rates Google Vertex's global endpoint also lists. Google lists $4, $20 and $0.20 cache reads from 2026-12-01; OpenRouter lists no cache-write rate for that date yet, so cache writes then bill at input. Through 2026-11-30, cache writes bill at input plus five minutes of Google's cache storage ($2.25 per million tokens per hour, so $0.1875); the endpoint lists only that storage part as its cache-write rate. From 2026-12-01 they bill at the new input plus five minutes of storage at twice that rate ($4.50 per million tokens per hour, so $0.375): $4.375. Neither Google nor OpenRouter lists Carbon's storage rate from that date (both read 2026-11-16), so it is taken to double like every other Carbon rate, as Google's own storage rates do when a model's token rates double (Gemini 3.8 Flash on the same page).
